title: Optimize prescription slate (wip)
content:
Goal
----
This doc captures the current wireframe + interaction notes for an Optimize UX concept we are calling the "Prescription Slate" — a focused panel that surfaces model-specific, actionable recommendations (batching, prefix caching, quantization) and turns them into one-click or guided changes for production routes.

Why a "prescription"?
- Users want clear, prioritized actions, not raw metrics.
- Each recommendation should include expected delta (cost, p99 latency, quality risk) and an easy rollback path.

High-level experience sketch
-------------------------
Panel placement: right rail on model route detail page (same surface as existing diagnostics)
Sections in the panel:
  1) Summary ribbon: single-line verdict (e.g., "Medium opportunity: ~34% token cost savings")
  2) Ranked prescriptions list (collapsible): each item is a card with severity pill, short description, expected impact, confidence score, quick actions
  3) Preview area: side-by-side simulation of a single request (before/after latency & cost & tokens)
  4) Change plan: quick apply (1-click) and guided apply (step-through with canary config)
  5) Audit notes & reasoning: short bullet list explaining how we estimated gains and risk vectors

Prescription card anatomy (fields)
- id: human-friendly short name (e.g., "prefix-cache:golden-boost")
- type: batching | caching | quant | routing
- cost_delta: friendly string (e.g., "-34% tokens / est $0.018 per 1k tokens saved")
- latency_delta: friendly string (e.g., "p99 +8ms" or "p50 -12ms")
- quality_risk: none | low | medium | high (tooltip with examples)
- confidence: 0-100% (model+telemetry)
- supporting_evidence: short bullets referencing traces/metrics/prompts
- quick_actions: ["Preview", "Apply to Canary", "Add to Playlist", "Dismiss"]

Example prescription (text-only preview)
- Title: "Enable prefix caching for FAQ-heavy routes"
- Type: caching
- Cost delta: "~-26% token cost for conversational flows; big wins on repeat prefixes"
- Latency delta: "p50 -6ms, p95 +2ms"
- Quality risk: "low (no prompt rewrite)"
- Confidence: "82% (histogram of repeated prefixes)"
- Evidence: "top 10 prefixes account for 42% of tokens; KV hits low currently"
- Action: [Preview] [Canary: 10%] [Apply] [Dismiss]

Preview workflow notes
- Preview runs a simulated token accounting using a sampled window (configurable, default 10k requests) and returns expected cost/latency deltas plus sample input/output snapshots.
- Must clearly mark that preview is an estimation (not exact). Provide link to raw sample set.

Apply / rollout mechanics
- Quick apply: applies recommended config directly to the route's non-production snapshot (saves to Draft). Requires explicit confirmation for production apply.
- Canary options: 1%, 5%, 10%, 25% with automatic metrics gating (cost, p95 latency, quality regression on evaluation set).
- Automatic fallback: if canary shows >3% quality regression or latency > SLO threshold for 5m, rollback automatically and notify the owner.

Quantization prescription specifics
- Show quant format recommended (e.g., 4-bit, q4_0, dynamic quant) and note hardware compatibility (Dedicated pools vs Hosted).
- Show expected model size reduction and expected per-token cost reduction.
- Include a compatibility check: list of downstream features that may be impacted (function calling, streaming).

Batching prescription specifics
- Recommend batch size policy change and/or use of continuous batching window.
- Simulation shows throughput lift and latency tail impact.
- UI exposes toggle for "latency-first" vs "throughput-first" profiles and shows which jobs/routes would be affected.

Dismiss / feedback loop
- Every dismissed prescription should collect a short reason (pre-populated options + free text) to feed model improvements and pruning rules.
- We will store dismissal reasons as signals for the Optimize model.

Wireframe ascii (very rough)
[Model Route Detail page] | [Prescriptions Slate]
-------------------------+---------------------------
Route header             | Summary ribbon: Medium opportunity
Route metrics            | Card 1: Prefix caching (82% confidence)  [Preview][Canary]
(usage, p95, token cost) | Card 2: Batch window -> 64ms (low risk) [Preview][Apply]
                         | Card 3: Quantize -> q4_0 (Dedicated only) [Preview][Add to Playlist]
                         | Preview area: sample in/out, cost table

Backlog grooming seeds (tickets)
- OPT-1201: Prescription ranking algorithm (telemetry + heuristics) - priority P0
- OPT-1202: Preview simulation engine (sample selection + offline estimator) - P0
- OPT-1203: Canary gating framework integration (playbooks + auto-rollback) - P1
- OPT-1204: Dismissal UX + telemetry capture - P2
- OPT-1205: Quant compatibility matrix UI + validators - P1

Acceptance criteria (for MVP)
- Panel appears on route detail and surfaces at least 3 actionable prescriptions for routes in dataset A.
- Preview simulation executed and returns cost/latency delta within 15% of observed when applied to a held-out test.
- Canary apply uses existing rollout APIs and supports automatic rollback.
- Dismiss reasons are recorded in telemetry and viewable in Optimize analytics.

Open questions / decisions
- Should prescriptions be auto-created nightly or only when user requests an analysis? (ops cost tradeoff)
- How aggressive should confidence thresholds be before surfacing high-impact quantization changes?
- UI copy: do we use medical metaphors (prescription, patient) or neutral (recommendation, action)? Product leaning: neutral language preferred but team feedback needed.

Notes for engineering handoff
- Backend needs an endpoint that returns a ranked list of prescriptions with proofs references (log sample ids, histogram snapshots). Keep payload small for fast UI render.
- Preview route should be implemented as an async job (queue + progress UI) to avoid blocking the page.
- Canary application uses the existing rollout API; add an opt-in param that tags the change as "optimize-prescription" for audit.

Next steps (this sprint)
- PM: finalize ranking heuristics doc (owner: Maya) - due EOD Thu
- Design: iterate on card visual weight and severity color palette (owner: Luca) - mid-sprint review
- Eng: spike on preview estimator and sample selector (owner: Priya) - demo Wednesday

Slack thread refs
- #optimize-prescriptions (link: slack://channel?id=CD24F2G)

Related docs & inspirations
- CONFLUENCE-OPTIMIZE-4521: past experiments on prefix caching
- past UX: see github.com/redwood-inference/optimize-ui/issues/87 for earlier mockups

Notes to reviewer
- This is intentionally sketchy; focus feedback on the workflow friction points: preview fidelity, canary granularity, and dismissal signal quality.
- Please add concrete examples of routes you think should *not* be auto-prescribed (e.g., low-volume premium routes).
